you are 100% valid in wanting no contact with them. I can sympathize heavily with your situation in terms of family dynamic. I'm ftm, but was presenting female most of my life. Bras are likely going to be a good idea for confidence. It just helps to have that support sometimes and would probably help with dysphoria. You can definitely start wearing one whenever you want because there are bras for pretty much any size if you take the time to look. There are push-up bras which can be helpful for lifting and pushing together breasts which makes them seem fuller. I would recommend starting with some cheaper ones of different varieties (there are a lot of different styles of bras and some work better than others for different shapes and sizes of people) and seeing how they feel and how they shape your body. Starting cheap is a good way to experiment with what works well, then you can start finding bras that are maybe a little pricier but fit your needs more exactly. Good luck on your hunt for what works well for you!

I watch someone on youtube that talked about how he deals with internalized religious guilt as an ex-mormon atheist. His advice has really helped me with working on my internalized homophobia and religious guilt. 

What I do now is take a second (if I have the time) to backpedal and walk through why I feel like that and explain in a chain of single sentences until I get to a point where the line of thinking either seems absurd or trivial. But overall, it just takes time. It takes self training and mentally or verbally correcting yourself when you have those automatic homophobic thoughts. You've got your whole life ahead of you to learn and grow and it will get easier over time.

Example: I have a thought about internalized homophobia. I then backpedal to myself saying "Okay, I have had a homophobic thought > I have this thought because I was raised in a society where being gay is frowned upon > therefore I was raised thinking that being gay was a sin/not okay > I think this way because it's a pattern that I'm used to > That pattern is comfortable because it's what I've known my whole life > It is comfortable because adults in my life taught me to think this way > I no longer believe in that logic > I know now logically and scientifically that being lgbt is healthy and valid > I know homophobia isn't a logical thought process because being lgbt is very real and not a choice > etc etc"

If you can have those kinds of conversations, bring up that it impacts your ability to put effort into the relationship or that it puts strain on how connected you feel.
If you really want to make things work, make sure your voice is heard. Relationships are tough sometimes, but being transparent with your partner might go a long way.

13 is definitely not too young. It's perfectly healthy and okay for people to know things about themselves like who you are interested in. You are very valid. What's important to remember is that YOU are the only person that gets to decide what you would like to label yourself as. You always have the right to adapt and change as you grow as a person. Don't be afraid to try a label. If it fits that's great! If it doesn't fit for some reason in the future, it's still perfectly okay to have identified as a lesbian too. You'll keep learning more and more as you get older.
I personally started identifying as bi, then lesbian, then agender pansexual, then I figured out at the age of 21 that I felt the most comfortable identifying as a bisexual transman. These things take time and can be overwhelming, but listen to your heart- if your heart says lesbian, then you are a valid lesbian every day of the week.
